title: The Veil of Moses
lead: After speaking with the LORD on Sinai, Moses's face shone, and he wore a veil when he was not in God's presence (Exodus 34:29-35). Paul reads the story in 2 Corinthians 3 as a picture of the glory of the first covenant, of the veil that lies on the reading of Moses, and of the removal of the veil when someone turns to the Lord.

sections.b: In Exodus, Moses came down with the second tablets, his face shone, the people were afraid, and he put a veil over his face except when he went in before the LORD. The Hebrew verb for "shone" (qaran) is related to the word for "horn," which led to Moses being shown with horns in Latin art.

Paul says the glory was being set aside, that the veil hid the end of it, and that a veil still lies on the minds of those who read Moses without turning to the Lord. He ends with hope: the veil is taken away when one turns, and all believers see the glory with unveiled faces. Scholars debate whether Paul means the veil is on Jews as such, on all who read without the Spirit, or on his rivals' reading of Moses.
